t: A paramount chiefdom of some 30 Algonquian peoples in coastal Virginia, built by Wahunsenacah, whom the English called Powhatan.
It met the founders of Jamestown in 1607 and nearly destroyed the colony in 1609–1610 and again in 1622.
Defeated in 1646, its peoples became tributaries of Virginia; the Pamunkey and Mattaponi keep reservations confirmed in 1677.
dyk: Some of the first Native American words to enter English came from Powhatan, among them raccoon, moccasin, tomahawk and persimmon.
ev: Spanish Jesuits found the Ajacán mission, destroyed by local people the next year
Wahunsenacah kills the chief of the Kecoughtan and installs his son
The English found Jamestown; John Smith is brought before Wahunsenacah
Pocahontas marries John Rolfe, ending the First Anglo-Powhatan War
Opechancanough’s coordinated attacks kill some 347 colonists
Opechancanough is captured; the Treaty of 1646 makes the Powhatan tributaries
Cockacoeske signs the Treaty of Middle Plantation

f.capital: Werowocomoco (to 1609); Orapax (from 1609); Matchut (by 1614); later Pamunkey towns under Opechancanough
f.predecessor: Six chiefdoms inherited by Wahunsenacah: Powhatan, Arrohateck, Appamattuck, Pamunkey, Youghtanund and Mattaponi
f.successor: Tributary tribes of the Colony of Virginia, led by the Pamunkey
